features.summary: 73 keys, E1–E7, 43 white / 30 black, with the E-to-E black key pattern and measured geometry.
Six ordered sections at the corrected v1.2.0 fractions, the 54/46 deck/keybed split, and one continuous chassis.
147 stable control IDs, per-section landmarks and density, and Program and Synth as the only primary OLEDs.
Pointer, independent multi-touch, glissando, cancel, blur and focused-key Space/Enter press and release.
Every visible control moves or presses and reports its declared functional state; operating every decorative control leaves the audio graph untouched and the rendered output silent.
Roles, accessible names, min/max/value/valuetext, orientation, keyboard operation, labelled regions and visible focus.
Note on/off on rendered audio, repeated and overlapping notes, per-note release shortening the tail, all-notes-off, and node cleanup back to baseline.
Pointer, multi-touch, mapped computer keyboard with repeat suppression, MIDI note/velocity/CC64/all-notes-off, and denied, unsupported and disconnected MIDI states.
Sustain transitions measured on the rendered tail, concurrent voices, deterministic stealing order, polyphony cap, and velocity moving level and filter in the expected direction.
Truthful ready/idle/unsupported/error status and its display, plus blur, MIDI disconnect and unmount stopping every owned voice and closing the context.
No marketing hero or reference image, rail and keybed attached inside one chassis, instrument at 88–97% of a 1440x900 viewport with no vertical scroll, and full width without clipping at 390x844.

Six selectable types with a playable model each; Grand, Upright and Electric are the bundled recordings in public/samples/, loaded through the asset boundary from disk with no network, decoded, played, and shown to be audibly distinct from each other and from the three synthesised types; the manifest's provenance, licences, root coverage and file list are asserted against the files that actually ship.

Two layers with independent enable, level, octave shift, piano type and effect chain; one voice per enabled layer with separate ownership, release and cleanup; focus follows the layer and swaps the panel's banked values.

KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre (including the electric-only Dyno settings), Unison, Soft Release, String Res, Section On and Master Level each measurably change rendered audio in the documented direction, and agree with the panel's own state.

Sustain from the UI button, the computer keyboard and MIDI CC64, measured on the rendered tail; SUSTPED routes the pedal per layer; pedal-up releases with the longer damper. Soft and sostenuto pedals are not implemented and are declared unsupported rather than approximated.

A failing or absent asset boundary reports the failure, keeps the keybed playable on the labelled synthesised fallback, and never reports the recorded library as ready; synthesised types are not reported as a fallback at all.

One AudioContext with per-layer buses and chains in the documented order, a shared rotary, master gain, wave-shaper limiter and exactly one destination connection; silence before the first note, master mute silencing every configuration, and every node returned to baseline after cleanup and to zero after dispose.

FX focus follows layer focus and the manual focus button, per-layer banks, Piano group mode, Delay/Comp/Reverb global mode, per-unit bypass, the all-effects bypass being identical to no unit on, To Rotary moving a layer off the piano bus, and Reverb preceding the Rotary.

Every unit and every listed type processes real audio: Mod 1 and Mod 2 (six types each, pairwise distinct), Delay with tempo, feedback, dry/wet and a feedback filter that dulls successive repeats without touching the dry path, Amp Sim/EQ (three amps, two 24 dB filters, three EQ bands, drive), Compressor, Reverb (six types, decay growing Booth to Cathedral, tone, fully wet at max) and the shared Rotary (slow/fast, drive, smooth acceleration).

Every Phase 1 test file is still present and green against the Phase 2 engine; the surface, keybed geometry, input behaviour and decorative-control contract are unchanged for the sections this phase does not touch.

Store and recall restore every supported piece of state — panel values, per-layer banks, octaves, focus, splits, zones, scenes, morphs, clock and transpose — across the 32 slots, and the dirty indicator is computed from the stored program rather than tracked, so it cannot lie in either direction.

STORE arms, auditions the destination and confirms on the second press; STORE AS names first with the dial and the page buttons; the 8 Live slots auto-store every edit and survive a reload through an injectable storage boundary.

Selecting another program discards the unstored edit and coming back restores the stored values, and SHIFT cancels an armed STORE without writing anything. No undo is claimed: the Solo/Undo button is declared unsupported with the spec clause that excludes it, and a test asserts it changes nothing.

The eight program buttons, the two page buttons, the endless dial in both directions, and the numeric list view from SHIFT + dial or the PROG VIEW button, with browsing still live while the list is open.

Enable, level, octave and effect target asserted for each of the seven layers of the three engines, with the enable state confirmed on rendered audio, an effect edit landing on the focused layer and not its sibling, one shared chain for the two organ layers and three independent chains for the three synth layers.

The eleven documented split positions, every one of them reachable from the editor with the ends as stops; three points making four zones; a layer walked into each zone with note routing asserted at both boundaries; Off/±6/±12 crossfade gains; and a note outside a layer zone building no voice at all.

Wheel and Control Pedal assignment latched from the source button, every destination interpolated at the source position (one rising while another falls), the morphed value reaching the engine, the panel indicating assigned destinations, and SHIFT + source clearing that source only.
Scene I and II hold two layer-enable configurations while sharing every sound parameter, and each scene keeps its own state when the other is edited.

Two organ layers: full note lifecycle with repeated note-on not stacking voices and every voice and node returning to baseline after release, per-layer level and keyboard zone, focus following the panel, one shared effect chain and one output, and cleanup on dispose.

B3, Vox, Farf and Pipe 1 rendered audibly distinct from each other and separated by measured harmonic content, the printed B3 footages and the two documented reuse models, drawbars as real levels that change the spectrum of a ringing note, Farfisa registers switching past half travel, single-triggered percussion with its volume/decay/harmonic options, key click, and vibrato separated from chorus and deepening across 1-2-3. The nine drawbars, their footages and their LED/indicator state are asserted on the panel itself.

The organ routed into the shared rotary speaker, slow/fast ramping through acceleration rather than switching, Stop Mode decelerating to a standstill, drive, close mic, and a morphable speed driven from the wheel.

Three synth layers, the exact required waveform list, five categories rendered audibly distinct, every Pure waveform given its own spectrum including both pulse widths and noise, and Osc Ctrl acting per category while leaving Pure alone.

LP12, LP24, HP and BP mapped onto different biquad stacks and rendered differently from each other; cutoff, resonance, keyboard tracking, drive and envelope amount each moving the rendered spectrum; and the oscillator, filter and amplifier envelopes shaping audio as three separate effects, with decay at maximum acting as sustain.

Poly, mono and legato voice allocation, note priority with several keys held, glide between legato notes, unison stacking, vibrato only when a vibrato source is selected, pitch-stick bend on sounding voices, five LFO waveforms modulating each destination with an off state and master-clock sync, and the two unimplemented synth modes muting instead of faking.

A deterministic step order for every direction and range, steps fired in order on an injected clock and stopping when switched off, Gate mode gating every held note at once, real audio gated through the engine with ARP RUN, KB Hold holding notes, and the rate locking to the master clock when sync is on.

One AudioContext with every section built on the context it was handed, one destination connection and one master path that nothing bypasses, sections switching off independently, every voice and node released on dispose, and programs, scenes, zones, morphs, the master clock, transpose and Panic reaching all three engines through the same panel state.

Every one of the 138 functional controls is operated and must change either the settings the engine is driven from or deck state outside its own position (its own value and its layer bank are excluded from the comparison, so a control that only remembers itself fails). The four modal controls that retarget the next action are declared and asserted individually. The nine decorative controls are listed with the spec clause that excludes each, and operating them changes nothing at all.

Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 test still passes unchanged except four assertions that encoded a Phase 2 truth (that the Organ, Synth and Program sections were decorative in their entirety); each keeps its invariant restated against the true decorative set, and each is documented in evidence/stage3-visual-audit.md.

notes: Audio behaviour is asserted on real rendered signals: src/audio/offline.ts is a deterministic offline Web Audio implementation that evaluates oscillators, buffer playback, parameter automation, audio-rate modulation, biquads, delay lines, wave shapers and stereo panning sample by sample, because jsdom provides no Web Audio.

The recorded-sample tests read the very files that ship in public/samples/ through the same loader boundary the browser uses (src/test/engineRig.ts), so 'these three instruments sound different' is measured on the shipped assets rather than on fixtures.

Three groups of Phase 1 assertions were updated in place, and none was weakened: the engine's resting node count is now measured from the graph instead of hard-coded at 2 (the graph is bigger, the invariant is the same), the decorative-control assertions now check each control against its declared functional state and still require every Organ, Synth and Program control to be inert, and two status-text assertions follow the status strings that changed because what is true changed.
No test requires a physical MIDI device, network access or audio output.
